column1: # The black-box oracle tools of the tests, per CI platform; tools/testdata/oracles.py installs them.
# Columns: platform, package, version, method, source, sha256, path, provides
#   method  archive   download source (pinned by sha256), extract, put <path> on PATH ("inner!dir" extracts the
#           deb       download source (pinned), install it with apt; <path> is the directory of its executables
#           macpkg    download a dmg (pinned) and install the package inside it; <path> as for deb
#                     install the packages of <source> (space separated) with the platform's package manager;
#                     their versions are whatever the manager holds and are recorded by "oracles.py versions";
#                     <path> is "-" or a directory to add to PATH ("brew:<formula>/bin" names a keg)
#           build     download source (pinned) and build <package> with the recipe of oracles.py; <path> is "-"
#           script    run the build script <source> (a path from the repository root) with the prefix
#                     ~/.smalt/<package>-<version>, whose bin directory goes on PATH; CI caches it apart, keyed
#   provides  the executables the row puts on PATH, comma separated; "name=file" installs file under name.
# Versions: every runner has the same version of every tool a test runs. ffmpeg is 7.1.2 (the clips and the
# swscale-based color tests need 7.1; 7.1.1 decodes some small H.264 pictures wrongly on arm64) with the components of
# builds it and each of those libraries from pinned source releases on every runner (under MSYS2 on Windows), as no
# prebuilt 7.1.2 has all of them (Ubuntu's and BtbN's lack libvo_amrwbenc and libspeex, Homebrew's libvo_amrwbenc,
# and gyan.dev's full builds stop at 7.1.1).
# libwebp 1.6.0, exiftool 13.59, libjxl 0.11.2 and libjpeg-turbo 3.1.3 come from official builds where one exists;
# libjxl is built from source on Linux arm64 (no release build) and macOS (Homebrew's version moves), libjpeg-turbo
# on Windows (its official build there is an installer). OpenJPEG is 2.5.3, the version Smalt's JPEG 2000 codec
# ports, built from source on Linux and macOS without -ffast-math (which OpenJPEG's own Release configuration and
# therefore the official Linux and macOS builds use) and without fused multiply-adds: the irreversible wavelet is
# float arithmetic, and both reorder it (the official Windows build does neither). libtiff 4.7.1 (Ubuntu's 4.5
# writes byte-swapped float strips wrongly) and FLAC 1.5.0 are built from source everywhere, against the codec
# libraries of the platform's package manager. The container validators of the test kit run GPAC's MP4Box, TSDuck's
# tsp, mkvalidator and mkvmerge where they are installed (MP4Box's version is the package manager's, recorded, not
# pinned); mkvalidator is built on Windows only, as its project builds it, since its GCC build misreads Seek
# elements and crashes on every file; sox and opus-tools are used by no test; smalt-gifenc drives the encoder of
# giflib 5.2.2 (MIT, tools/testdata/gif-oracle); smalt-alacenc drives the encoder of Apple's ALAC library at its last
# commit, c38887c (Apache-2.0, tools/testdata/alac-oracle); smalt-mpeg4ref is the MPEG-4 Visual reference decoder of ISO/IEC
# 14496-5 (version 2.3, 2000-12-13, from the Internet Archive's copy of ISO's Publicly Available Standards), built by
# tools/testdata/mpeg4-oracle/build.py with g++ (Homebrew's on macOS, whose clang rejects the pre-standard C++);
# smalt-mpeg2ref is the MPEG-2 video reference decoder (smalt-mpeg2dec, with Smalt's inverse DCT) and encoder
# (smalt-mpeg2enc) of ISO/IEC 13818-5 (MSSG version 1.2, from the Internet Archive's copy of ISO's Publicly
# Available Standards), built by tools/testdata/mpeg2-oracle/build.py with the platform's C compiler;
# ImageMagick comes from apt on Linux (convert), from Homebrew on macOS (magick) and with the Windows runner image;
# OpenJPH 0.21.3, the HTJ2K oracle, is built from source everywhere without its SIMD kernels; GPAC publishes no
# pinnable Windows build, so MP4Box is not provisioned on Windows.
# The gain map oracles are built from source everywhere: libultrahdr 1.4.0 (ultrahdr_app) with its scalar kernels and
# its lookup tables of the transfer functions and gains turned off, and libavif 1.3.0 (avifgainmaputil, avifdec)
# decoding through the package manager's dav1d, with libxml2 for JPEG XMP except on Windows.
